sections.h2: Where does Bertie County record deeds, and what are the hours?
sections.html:
Deeds are recorded in Windsor, in the courthouse at King and Dundee streets, where the register's office occupies the first floor. Visitors use 108 Dundee Street; mail goes to PO Box 340, Windsor, NC 27983.

Staff are in from 8:30 to 5:00, but the recording cutoff is 4:30 every day, so a deed delivered at a quarter to five sits until the next morning. Electronic recording is accepted now, which lets a closing attorney send the deed without a drive to Windsor. Holidays and bad weather can close the doors.

sections.h2: What does the register keep, and why does recording matter?
sections.html:
The register looks after deeds, deeds of trust, powers of attorney, assumed names, plats, maps and military discharge papers. Voters pick the register every two years, and the office answers to Chapter 161 of the General Statutes.

Recording gives a buyer priority. Under G.S. 47-18, an unrecorded conveyance has no force against lien creditors or purchasers who paid value, and the order of registration sets who ranks first. Until the deed is filed in the county where the land lies, the buyer is exposed to a competing claim.

  • Records are filed by name, so the office cannot look up an owner from a street address.
  • For an address search, call the tax assessor's mapping line at (252) 794-5311.
  • Anyone may obtain copies of recorded papers in person, by mail or by phone request, except military discharge forms, which have limited access.

sections.h2: How much does the Windsor office charge to file a deed?
sections.html:
The office follows the uniform statewide schedule in G.S. 161-10 and prints it on the county fee page. A standard instrument costs $26.00 through page 15, with $4.00 added per page beyond that. A deed of trust or mortgage runs $64.00 through page 35 on the same $4.00 add-on.

  • Second instrument in one document: $10.00
  • Format failure: $25.00 on top of the filing fee
  • Satisfaction of a mortgage: no charge

The fee is paid before filing, and the statute treats the schedule as the only filing charge. For an odd page count, phone (252) 794-5309 first.

sections.h2: What state tax does the seller hand over when the deed is filed?
sections.html:
The seller owes the state excise tax: $1.00 per $500 of price or value, counting a fractional $500 as a whole one. Payment goes to the register ahead of recording.

Receipts are divided in half between the county general fund and the Department of Revenue. A parcel in two counties is taxed in the one holding more of its value. The closing attorney calculates the amount from the contract price.

sections.h2: What do Bertie County's own recording rules require?
sections.html:
A resolution adopted in April 1991 under G.S. 161-30 took effect June 1, 1991. The register may not take any map or instrument affecting real property unless two items appear on its face: a name and address for returning the document, and the grantee's permanent mailing address.

Format rules apply as well. The county posts them for filers: letter or legal paper, black type on white, nothing below 9 point, one side only, and a 3 inch blank band at the top of page one. A paper that misses the format is still recorded once the $25.00 non-standard fee is paid, and the register may waive the fee for a slightly small but legible font.

Before you send a deed to Windsor, confirm that it is signed and notarized, that both addresses appear on page one, and that the fee and transfer tax are ready.

sections.h2: Why do Bertie County's old land records reach so far back?
sections.html:
Bertie Precinct became a county in 1722, when it separated from Chowan County, and the register's land and grant records start that same year. The original county was large. It took in what are now Tyrrell, Edgecombe, Northampton and Hertford counties, and by 1780 it had been divided into roughly its present shape.

For a seller with an inherited farm tract, that history matters. A chain of title that begins in colonial grants may run through Bertie books even when the land now lies in a neighboring county, so a title search can reach back much farther than the online window. The online index starts in 1977 and also supports a search by book number from Book 600, so call the office about anything older.

sections.h2: What else happens at the Windsor counter on closing day?
sections.html:
The register's staff also issue marriage licenses, swear in notaries, and sell birth and death certificates, so the counter can be busy. A marriage license applicant must arrive before 4:00 p.m., an hour ahead of the recording cutoff. Notary oaths need no appointment, and a new notary may bring the green transmittal letter from the Secretary of State.

Two items at the counter are cash only: the $60.00 marriage license and the $24.00 statewide birth certificate service for people born anywhere in North Carolina from 1971 onward. Ask when you call how the office wants payment for a recording.

sections.h2: How are names changed on a Bertie County deed?
sections.html:
A new deed has to be drawn up, and the register's FAQ sends owners to an attorney for it. After signing and notarization, the deed is brought to the office with the fee.

A land contract works differently. Under Chapter 47H, the seller must record the contract, or a short memorandum of it, within five business days, and the purchaser can cancel until midnight of the third business day after signing.

Paid-off loans leave a loose end. Ask the lender for a satisfaction and have it recorded, which costs nothing and clears the title check before a sale.

sections.h2: How does the register fit into a Bertie County sale?
sections.html:
The closing attorney or title agent searches the records, files the new deed and any new deed of trust, and pays the transfer tax from the settlement. Most sellers never visit the office themselves.

Property taxes are the one title item that lives elsewhere. Unpaid bills are a lien and are cleared with the tax collector, as covered in our Bertie County property tax guide. Gaps from older paperwork, such as a mortgage never released or an estate never opened, get fixed by recording the missing document before closing.

One courthouse serves the whole county. Windsor was founded in 1766 and named seat of government in 1774, and a parcel in any of the eight towns, from Askewville and Aulander in one direction to Roxobel and Powellsville in another, is recorded at the same counter. Attorneys who record electronically skip the drive to Dundee Street altogether.

faqs.q: What number reaches the Bertie County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: Call (252) 794-5309, or send a fax to (252) 794-5374. The office is at 108 Dundee Street in Windsor.

faqs.q: What is the last time to record a deed in Bertie County?
faqs.a: Recording closes at 4:30 p.m., thirty minutes before the office does. Electronic recordings are accepted too.

faqs.q: What is the price of recording a standard Bertie County deed?
faqs.a: Through 15 pages the charge is $26.00, then $4.00 for each extra page. A deed of trust costs $64.00 through 35 pages.

faqs.q: Which party pays the excise tax on a Bertie County sale?
faqs.a: The seller, who sends $1.00 per $500 of value to the register before the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: How do I find the owner of a Bertie County street address?
faqs.a: Call the tax assessor's mapping office at (252) 794-5311. The register indexes by name, so an address alone will not work there.
